newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent crude extends London's late slide.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent crude extends London's late slide.

text.p: SIMEX Brent crude futures fell on Thursday, as profits gained on OPEC overnight were further eroded, traders said.
August was last traded at $18.16 per barrel, down six cents from the London settlement overnight.
London rose to $18.45 on the IPE after OPEC said it would freeze for six months its 25.033 million barrels per day (bpd) supply ceiling, adding members had pledged to adhere to quotas.
However, by the close London had simmered to $18.22 for a gain on the day of 35 cents.
NYMEX followed a similar course on ACCESS.
August was last traded in Asia at $19.43, nine cents below New York where the contract had gained 49 cents to close at $19.52.
"Any rally is a chance to sell the market down. London will look to test $18.00 later," one broker said.
He said the rise on OPEC was based on a a knee jerk reaction. Longer term there was little belief OPEC would maintain quotas because of its poor track record on quota discipline.
